title: Government to Stay Live on Mobile: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches New Portal for Farmers
subtitle:
Farmers to Access All Agricultural Schemes on Their Mobile Phones: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Farmers to Get Direct Access to Government Assistance Without Visiting Offices: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Single Portal for All Ministry Services to Empower Farmers Digitally: Union Agriculture Minister
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Digital India and his commitment to farmers’ welfare, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today formally launched the upgraded Agri Welfare Portal. The portal aims to provide farmers across the country with direct, easy access to government schemes, financial assistance and reliable agricultural information on their mobile phones, eliminating procedural hurdles and the role of intermediaries.
Addressing the launch programme, Shri Chouhan said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s clear vision is to ensure that the government remains accessible to citizens and farmers at all times through their mobile phones. Technology, he said, could fulfil its true purpose only when it reached farms and rural communities and made farmers’ lives easier. With the upgraded portal, farmers will no longer need to visit multiple government offices or navigate different websites to obtain information about schemes or submit applications. The platform will also bring together Farmer Producer Organisations, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, agricultural scientists, researchers and startups, creating a common digital platform for the wider agricultural ecosystem. Emphasising the importance of reliable information, Shri Chouhan directed officials to ensure that the portal remained accurate and regularly updated. He said outdated or incomplete information could undermine public trust in the system, making continuous updates essential to its success. He also stressed that the language and processes must be simple enough for small and marginal farmers, including those with limited formal education, to understand and use the platform with ease. To help farmers make effective use of the portal and other digital tools, a special training campaign will be conducted through Krishi Vigyan Kendras across the country.
Shri Chouhan also commended the entire technical team for developing the upgraded portal within the stipulated time. Developed in compliance with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology’s Digital Brand Identity Manual 3.0 and Guidelines for Indian Government Websites 3.0, the portal is designed to offer a secure, mobile-friendly and accessible digital experience, including for persons with disabilities. The platform will serve as a single-window gateway to major government initiatives, including PM-KISAN, AgriStack and the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, making it easier for farmers to access relevant services and information through a common interface. Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, Additional Secretary Pramod Meherda, senior officials from the Digital Agriculture Division and other officials from the Ministry and the National Informatics Centre were present at the launch.
Key Benefits of the Agri Welfare Portal
All services in one place: Information on the Ministry’s schemes, subsidies, rules and digital services will be available on a single portal, reducing the time and effort farmers spend navigating multiple platforms.
Greater transparency and fewer intermediaries: Online eligibility checks, direct application facilities and the transfer of financial assistance through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) will make processes more transparent and reduce the role of intermediaries.
Designed for rural connectivity: Built with rural users in mind, the portal is lightweight and user-friendly, enabling smooth operation on basic smartphones and in areas with weak internet connectivity.
Timely and reliable agricultural information: Farmers will be able to access authentic information on weather conditions, scientific farming practices, the availability of seeds and fertilisers, and prevailing market prices for agricultural produce.
Accessible to persons with disabilities: Designed in line with modern government accessibility standards, the portal supports screen readers and simple navigation, enabling visually impaired users and other persons with disabilities to access its services more easily.

title: India–New Zealand FTA to Come into Force on 20th October 2026 on Vijay Dashmi, Opening New Opportunities for Indian Exporters
subtitle:
100% Duty-Free Access to New Zealand Market to Create Opportunities for Indian MSMEs, Artisans, Farmers and Women Entrepreneurs: lUnion Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal

India Flags Off First-Ever JCB Machine Export to New Zealand

New Zealand Commits to Facilitate USD 20 Billion Investment into India under India–New Zealand FTA
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri
Piyush
Goyal
and New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment, Hon. Todd McClay, today jointly announced through a virtual conference that the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) will enter into force on 20 October 2026, on the occasion of Vijay
Dashmi, a day symbolising victory and new beginnings..
Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri
Piyush
Goyal
said, “Ours is a winning partnership, both on and off the field. The success of this agreement will be measured by the opportunities it creates and the difference it makes to the lives of the people of New Zealand and India. For India, 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market opens significant new opportunities for our exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers, and women entrepreneurs. For our farmers, the agreement combines new opportunities with appropriate safeguards. The Agricultural Productivity Partnership, with action plans for apples, kiwifruit and honey, establishment of Centres of Excellence, promote better orchard management, reduce post-harvest losses, and improve agricultural productivity, supporting stronger farm incomes across the country. The agreement also aligns with the vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister for
Viksit
Bharat
2047: that is a developed and prosperous India built on competitiveness, innovation, productive capacity, and inclusive prosperity when India celebrates 100 years of independence.”
New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment, Hon. Todd McClay, stated, “The entry into force of India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement is a watershed moment in the relationship between our two countries. For New Zealand exporters, the FTA opens the door to 1.4 billion consumers and one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies. New Zealand’s current exports to India will benefit from tariff elimination or substantial tariff reductions. At the same time, all Indian goods will be able to enter New Zealand duty-free, creating new opportunities for Indian exporters and placing them on a level playing field with New Zealand’s other FTA partners. The success of this agreement will ultimately be measured by the opportunities it creates and the extent to which our businesses use it.”
Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, said, “FTAs are about creating a deep economic partnership between countries. As a part of the FTA, we see this partnership also driving a lot of New Zealand investment in India. All the other big economies around the Pacific have got a much deeper trade with New Zealand. This FTA opens up the opportunity that we can also be a major contributor to the bilateral trade between India and New Zealand. The job is now to translate this opportunity into actual benefits for our people. We are working with all the Industry and the associations to take this message forward to every district across the country.”
Under the leadership of
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India and New Zealand have continued to deepen and expand their engagement. The FTA reflects India’s commitment to forging partnerships with developed economies that deliver market access, create employment opportunities and empower youth, women and MSMEs, in line with the vision of
Viksit
Bharat 2047
Representatives from industries in India and New Zealand also participated in the ceremony and spoke about opportunities created by the Agreement for their respective sectors, including services, footwear, engineering and agriculture.
On the occasion, the first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off by the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry. Flag-offs of a range of products across the agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather sectors are also planned for the entry-into-force day. These initiatives reflect the confidence of Indian manufacturers and the opportunities the Agreement opens up for exporters across the country.
New Zealand has eliminated customs duties on all tariff lines covering Indian exports, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%. Textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, automobiles and auto components, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, agricultural products and processed foods are expected to benefit. Duty-free access for wooden logs, coking coal and metal waste and scrap will further strengthen manufacturing and MSME supply chains. The pharmaceutical and medical device industries will benefit from streamlined regulatory processes.
New Zealand has made its best services offer in any of its trade agreements to date, with market access in around 118 sectors and Most-Favoured-Nation commitments in about 139 sub-sectors. For the first time, it has also provided dedicated access in Health and Traditional Medicine Services, covering Ayurveda, Yoga and other AYUSH systems.
Indian youth and professionals will have access to a quota of 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas every year. There will be no numerical cap on Indian
students, with post-study work rights of up to three years for STEM Bachelor’s and Master’s graduates and up to four years for doctoral scholars.
The Agricultural Productivity Partnership is a key component of the Agreement, extending cooperation beyond tariff concessions to bring global technology, training and best practices to Indian farmers. It includes dedicated Action Plans for kiwifruit, apples and honey, with cooperation also extending to horticulture, forestry, livestock and fisheries.
New Zealand is providing technical assistance for establishing Centres of Excellence for kiwifruit, apples and honey. Under the Kiwifruit Action Plan, Phase I sites have been identified at
Pfutsero
in Nagaland and
Magra
in
Uttarakhand. Two further Centres of Excellence for apples are proposed in Himachal Pradesh and
Uttarakhand, while the Honey Action Plan envisages Centres of Excellence in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. These initiatives aim to support farmers through technology transfer, improved cultivation practices and enhanced productivity.
Representatives from Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland,
Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh, along with collaborating organisations from New Zealand, were present for the entry into force.
All Tariff Rate Quotas for apples, kiwifruit and
Mānuka
honey are formally linked to the delivery of the Action Plans, under the oversight of a Joint Agriculture Productivity Council. This links market access with farmer welfare.
New Zealand has committed to facilitate USD 20 billion of investment into India. The investment is expected to benefit agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups, and support innovation, entrepreneurship and employment generation under the Make in India vision.
To protect farmers, dairy producers,
fisherfolk
and rural communities, sensitive products such as dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions. Robust Rules of Origin, a bilateral safeguard mechanism and strong anti-circumvention provisions will ensure that the benefits flow only to genuine Indian exporters.
The Agreement opens an advanced overseas market to India’s MSMEs, women-led enterprises, start-ups, artisans and first-generation entrepreneurs. Zero duty and faster customs processes will lower landed costs and widen their customer base. Structured cooperation will provide enhanced access to trade-related information and linkages with New Zealand’s SME ecosystem, with a specific focus on enterprises owned by women and youth.
New Zealand has also committed to facilitate the registration of Indian Geographical Indications, opening avenues for protection of products associated with rural artisans and traditional industries.
The India–New Zealand FTA is a people-centric and inclusive partnership, anchored in the vision of
Viksit
Bharat 2047 and the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. It seeks to empower farmers, MSMEs, women-led enterprises, entrepreneurs, artisans, youth and professionals.
Negotiations were launched on 16 March 2025 and concluded on 22 December 2025, within nine months. The Agreement was signed on 27 April 2026. It supports the India–New Zealand Strategic Partnership: Roadmap to 2030, which sets an aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to NZ$7 billion (₹35,000 crore) by 2030.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards Organises Nationwide Interactive Sessions to Promote AYUSH with Quality Standards
subtitle:
Over 600 experts, practitioners and industry leaders participate

to advance standardization, safety, patient care, and international acceptance in the fields of AYURVEDA, YOGA, and SOWA-RIGPA
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major push towards standardisation in India’s traditional systems of medicine, the AYUSH Department of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) conducted two national events on standardization in Ayurveda, Yoga, and Sowa-Rigpa. By bridging traditional heritage with scientific quality control, BIS aims to boost consumer trust, and drive international recognition for the AYUSH sector. The nationwide campaign brought together over 600 key stakeholders including top researchers, industry pioneers, academic leaders, and practitioner:
PRAGATI 2026: National Seminar on Standardization in Ayurveda and Yoga
Hosted in Belagavi, Karnataka by BIS in association with KLE Shri BMK Ayurveda Mahavidyalaya and the KLE Academy of Higher Education & Research, PRAGATI 2026 brought together 600 participants to deliberate the role of Indian Standards in strengthening the Ayurveda and Yoga sectors. Ms. Shrishti Dixit, Scientist-E & Head (AYUSH), BIS, highlighted BIS’s work in formulating Indian Standards and expanding India's role in global standardization via ISO. During the seminar, the dignitaries emphasized that well-defined standards are vital for quality assurance, patient safety, credible research, and effective regulation. Key themes addressed during the seminar included:
Standardized Practice & Education:
Highlighting the need for uniform terminology, educational benchmarks, and clinical guidelines in Yoga and Ayurveda.
Industry & Start-up Support:
Guidance from industry leaders including Dr. Bindu Indira (Himalaya Wellness Company) and Dr. Srinivas Patil (Karnataka AYUSH Drugs Manufacturers Association) on how adopting BIS certification accelerates market access and builds consumer trust.
Interactive Open House:
Expert panel discussions led by Prof. (Dr.) Kashinath Samagandi (All India Institute of Ayurveda) and Vaidya Jayant Deopujari (Chairperson, Ayurveda Sectional Committee, BIS) interacyed with the delgates on
on practical issues in adopting standards across education, research, manufacturing and clinical practice, and discussed the gaps that need to be addressed for wider implementation.
ADVANCING SOWA-RIGPA STANDARDIZATION IN LEH, LADAKH
BIS convened a Brainstorming Session alongside its 5th Sowa-Rigpa Sectional Committee meeting at the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR) in Leh (UT of Ladakh). Delegates included Padma Shree Dr. Padma Gurmet (Chairperson of the BIS Sowa-Rigpa Sectional Committee and Founding Director of NISR), Dr. Arjun Singh (Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences), and Dr. Usama Akram (Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine) and Dr Mahe Alam from BIS. Deliberations focussed on -
Raw Material Quality & Safety:
Establishing rigorous testing parameters for single herbs, raw materials, and finished formulations along with
drug quality, safety and efficacy, laboratory and analytical requirements, pharmacopoeial standards and quality assurance.
IPR & Traditional Knowledge:
Safeguarding indigenous knowledge through patents, trademarks, and geographical indications for quality assessment
The initiatives were supported by premier national institutions, including the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), and Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS). BIS reaffirmed its commitment to continuously engage with industry and academia, facilitating simple online submission portals for new standardization proposals.
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the National Standard Body of India, responsible for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization, and conformity assessment. Through its dedicated Ayush Department, BIS is shaping quality standards that enable traditional Indian systems of medicine to achieve global excellence.

title: India to Host 61st Meeting of International Committee of Legal Metrology for the First Time in New Delhi from 26–28 October 2026
subtitle:
More than 100 international delegates and legal metrology experts to participate in the meeting

OIML Strategy Workshop and international seminar to deliberate on emerging technologies, digitalisation and the future of global legal metrology
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India will host the
61st Meeting of the International Committee of Legal Metrology (CIML)
for the first time from
26 to 28 October 2026 in New Delhi
. The meeting is being organised by the Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India, in association with the International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML).
The meeting is expected to bring together more than
100 international delegates and legal metrology experts
from across the world, including representatives of OIML Member States, Corresponding Member States and international organisations. Hosting the meeting for the first time marks a significant milestone in India's growing role in international cooperation, harmonisation of measurement standards, promotion of fair trade and consumer protection.
OIML Strategy Workshop and International Seminar
An international seminar on
“Evolutions in Legal Metrology”
will be organised on
26 October 2026
. The seminar will bring together experts from different countries to exchange experiences and best practices on the modernisation of legal metrology systems. Discussions will cover digitalisation of regulatory services, international harmonisation and recognition of measuring instruments, e-learning tools and innovative approaches to legal metrology administration.
An
OIML Strategy Workshop
will also be organised on
27 October 2026
, providing a platform for participating countries and international experts to deliberate on the future strategic direction and priorities of the organisation. Discussions are expected to cover emerging challenges, technological advancements, digital transformation, international cooperation and the evolving requirements of legal metrology systems worldwide.
Key Areas of Deliberation
During the three-day programme, CIML members will deliberate on important matters relating to the
development and revision of international recommendations, technical activities of the OIML, the OIML Certification System (OIML-CS), digital transformation, capacity building and international cooperation.
The meeting will facilitate the exchange of technical knowledge and experience among participating countries, supporting efforts to strengthen measurement systems and promote internationally recognised standards.
The 60th CIML Meeting was held on
13 and 15 October 2025 in Paris, France
, with representatives of 55 Member States present or represented, along with representatives of 12 Corresponding Members and five organisations in liaison. Key outcomes included the approval of technical publications relating to automated refractometers, weights and traffic speed meters, along with discussions on the framework for the OIML Certification System, digitalisation and international cooperation.
Strengthening India's Role in Global Legal Metrology
Hosting the 61st CIML Meeting provides India with
an opportunity to showcase its reforms and advancements in legal metrology
on an international platform. The Department of Consumer Affairs has undertaken several
initiatives to modernise the regulatory framework, simplify compliance procedures, promote trust-based regulation and facilitate Ease of Doing Business while ensuring robust consumer protection.
The meeting is expected to witness
participation from representatives of OIML Member States,
including France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Japan, China, Australia, Switzerland, the United States of America, South Africa and Brazil, among others. Representatives of Corresponding Members and associated international organisations are also expected to participate.
The diverse participation will provide opportunities to
exchange experiences, share best practices
and strengthen international cooperation in legal metrology. The meeting, along with the OIML Strategy Workshop and international seminar, will contribute to discussions on reliable measurements, fair trade, technological innovation and consumer confidence, while advancing India's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Benefits for Industry and Consumers
The meeting is expected to benefit Indian manufacturers by enhancing awareness of international measurement standards, conformity assessment requirements and the OIML Certification System. This can
support the development of quality products and facilitate access to international markets.
Greater
harmonisation of measurement requirements
can also help
reduce technical barriers to trade and avoid duplication in testing and certification,
where applicable. For consumers, reliable and accurate measurements are essential to ensuring fairness in transactions, correct quantity declarations and greater confidence in goods and services.
The event will also provide India with an opportunity to share its experience in regulatory reforms, digitalisation and Ease of Doing Business, while contributing to international discussions on modern and effective legal metrology systems.
International Cooperation in Legal Metrology
The International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML) is an intergovernmental organisation established in 1955 to promote the global harmonisation of legal metrology procedures. It develops international recommendations, standards and related documents for measuring instruments used in trade, industry, healthcare, safety and environmental protection.
The International Committee of Legal Metrology (CIML) is the principal decision-making body responsible for guiding the technical and administrative activities of the OIML. Its annual meeting provides a global platform for deliberations on policy matters, technical developments and international cooperation in legal metrology.
The hosting of the 61st CIML Meeting reinforces India's commitment to international collaboration and the development of harmonised measurement standards, supporting fair trade, consumer protection and confidence in measurement systems worldwide.

As a first, an observer delegation from New Zealand will also be participating in the exercise.
Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 will further strengthen military-to-military cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust between India and Australia. It will reinforce their shared commitment towards peace, stability and security in the Indo-Pacific region.

title: Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) and AcSIR announce partnership to advance Doctoral Research in Earth System Sciences
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 10:45AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) and the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR) declared a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) during a ceremony held on October 13, 2026, at Prithvi Bhawan Headquarters in New Delhi.
Under this landmark agreement, all ten premier research institutes under MoES have been recognized as AcSIR Associated Research Institutes (AcSIR-ARIs). The institutional collaboration integrates MoES’s state-of-the-art research facilities and scientific expertise with AcSIR’s flexible academic framework to offer doctoral (PhD) programs across diverse domains of earth system sciences including atmospheric, ocean, and polar sciences.
The MoU, which was executed on August 21, 2026, was signed by Dr. Praveen Kumar D., Scientist-G and Mission Director (Mission Mausam), on behalf of MoES, and Prof. Manoj Kumar Dhar, Director, AcSIR. The official declaration and document exchange were conducted in the presence of the Secretary, MoES, along with senior officials and directors from both organizations.
The Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala underscored the vital role of collaborative research and academic partnerships during an address marking a major national initiative between MoES, the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR).
The collaborative effort bridges MoES and its ten institutions with AcSIR, establishing a unified ecosystem for advanced scientific research and educational capacity building across oceanography, atmospheric sciences, hydrology, and planetary systems.
"I am sure MoES will be a big beneficiary — us, our institutions, our scientists, and the students who are actually engaging with earth sciences," stated the Secretary, MoES. "We really look forward to working with all institutions and their headquarters. We will ensure that this becomes a great association going forward for the benefit of the entire earth science faculty, science, and technology researchers."
The joint framework aims to foster interdisciplinary research, streamline resource and infrastructure sharing among national laboratories, and provide upgraded academic opportunities for early-career scientists and students.
Key Highlights of the Partnership
Nationwide network of recognized institutes
: All ten MoES institutes are operational as AcSIR-ARIs.
Academics and award of degree
: Students selected under AcSIR’s PhD program will conduct research at MoES institutes under the supervision of MoES scientists recognized as AcSIR faculty. AcSIR will award the doctoral degree, explicitly referencing the host institute on the degree certificate.
Operational readiness
: All ten institutes are participating in AcSIR's latest PhD enrolment cycle. Nodal AcSIR Coordinators have been appointed at each institute alongside a Central Coordinator at MoES to streamline academic operations.
Broad spectrum of research domains
: The collaboration opens doctoral opportunities in specialized fields of earth system sciences, including weather forecasting and climate services, numerical weather prediction, polar and cryosphere research, ocean observation and marine robotics, deep-sea mining and desalination, seismology and earthquake hazard assessment, coastal processes, marine living resources, and AI/ML applications in earth sciences.
Intellectual Property Rights
: IPR generated from research shall ensure crediting the student as inventor, while joint intellectual property being shared mutually.

title: DRI seizes 13 kg foreign-origin gold worth around Rs. 19.41 crore and dismantles a gold smuggling syndicate in Gujarat; three arrested
subtitle: Network ran through Ahmedabad and Surat airports, with an illegal melting unit in Vadodara with support from a Dubai-based financier
date:

content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has dismantled an organised gold smuggling syndicate that brought foreign-origin gold into India through Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad, and Surat International Airport. Three persons have been arrested under the Customs Act, 1962.
Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers kept the suspects under surveillance and carried out coordinated searches over 42 hours beginning 16 October 2026. The operation uncovered the full chain of the racket: smuggling by air passengers, hand-over to handlers, illegal melting, and sale through a jewellery outlet. It exposed dealings involving
13.017 kg foreign-origin gold valued at approximately Rs. 19.41 crore
, and three persons have been arrested.
Preliminary investigation revealed smuggling of gold into country through passengers using ingenious concealment methods. These included thin gold wires coated with rhodium, gold embedded in the inner linings of trolley bags, and gold paste concealed within the bags’ inner shells. After arrival, the gold was allegedly handed over to handlers outside the airports and routed through intermediaries to an illegal gold-melting facility in Vadodara. The melted gold was subsequently supplied to a jewellery shop in Ahmedabad for sale against cash.
Illegal gold melting facility
Rhodium coated wires
Gold paste
The coordinated operation led to the seizure of around
890 grams gold
and the recovery of incriminating evidences relating to
6.41 kg illegally melted gold
. Further searches at the jewellery shop resulted in the recovery of undocumented foreign-origin gold bars and records relating to dealings involving around
5.8 kg smuggled gold
routed through a separate handler linked to the syndicate’s main financier based in Dubai.
The operation exposed the interconnected roles of passengers, handlers, intermediaries, the gold-melting facility operator and the jewellery trade channel in facilitating the movement and disposal of smuggled gold. The handler/financier, the operator of the melting facility and other key persons were identified during the investigation. Three persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
The operation underscores DRI’s focused efforts to dismantle organised gold-smuggling networks by targeting every link, from concealment and airport movement to melting, financing and sale in the domestic market.

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will pay homage to the martyrs on Police Commemoration Day at National Police Memorial in New Delhi on Wednesday, 21st October 2026.
The Home Minister will flag-off a motorcycle rally of about 90 Police riders from States/UTs (Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi); Central Armed Police Forces (CRPF, CISF, BSF, SSB, ITBP and NSG) and some Central Police Organisations (RPF, NDRF and NIA). This is part of a nationwide rally themed ‘Fight Against Drugs’, wherein Police riders from all States/UTs and Central Forces would reach Ekta Nagar, Gujarat to join the Ekta Parade on October 31, 2026.
On October 21, 1959, ten valiant Policemen laid down their lives in an ambush laid by heavily armed Chinese troops at Hot Springs, Ladakh. Since then, October 21 is observed as Police Commemoration Day every year. In recognition of the sacrifices made by Police personnel and their paramount role in preserving national security and integrity, the Prime Minister dedicated National Police Memorial (NPM), Chanakyapuri, New Delhi to the nation on Police Commemoration Day-2018.
The Memorial gives Police Forces a sense of national identity, pride, unity of purpose, common history and destiny, besides reinforcing their commitment to protect the nation even at the cost of their lives. The Memorial comprises a Central Sculpture, the ‘Wall of Valour’ and a Museum. The Central Sculpture, which is a 30 feet high granite monolith cenotaph, stands for strength, resilience and selfless service of Police personnel. The Wall of Valour on which the names of martyrs are engraved stands as a steadfast acknowledgement of the bravery and sacrifice of Police personnel who have laid down their lives in the line of duty since Independence. The museum is conceptualized as a historical and evolving exhibition on policing in India. The Memorial is a site of pilgrimage, a place of reverence for Police personnel and citizen alike.  The NPM is open to public on all days except Mondays. Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) organise band display, parade and retreat ceremony at the NPM on every Saturday and Sunday in the evening, starting one hour prior to sunset.
On the lines of previous years, Police Commemoration Day, i.e., October 21, will be observed across the country to pay homage to police martyrs. The main function will be organised at National Police Memorial, New Delhi, where a joint parade of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Delhi Police would be held.  As per custom, the Union Home Minister will preside over the function. Union MoS (Home), MPs with Police background, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs amongst others will also pay homage to the martyrs by laying wreaths. Retired DGs, officers from Police fraternity and other dignitaries will also attend the event.
Apart from paying homage to the Police martyrs, Union Home Minister will address the assembly. The programme will conclude with Union Home Minister laying a wreath at the altar dedicated to the martyrs of Hot Springs. The event will be telecast live on Doordarshan, webcast on Police websites and covered by AIR and media.
As a part of the remembrances, CAPFs/CPOs will organise various Commemorative Events at NPM from October 22 to 30, which will include visits of family members of martyrs, Police Band Display, motorcycle rallies, Run for Martyrs, blood donation camps, essay/painting competitions for children and display of video films showcasing sacrifice, valour and services of Police personnel. Similar programmes will be organised by all the Police Forces across the country during this period.

He appreciated DoPT, Grih Kalyan Kendra and all officials associated with establishing the creche.

Through sustained monitoring, systematic records management, expeditious disposal of pending matters and active participation of officers and staff, the Department of Land Resources is making concerted efforts to achieve the objectives of Special Campaign 6. These initiatives reflect the Department’s continued commitment to institutionalizing Swachhata and fostering a clean, efficient, well-organized and responsive work environment.

title: CSIR-NIScPR Successfully Concludes Two-Week Skill Training Programme on Library Automation, Digitisation and Artificial Intelligence for Libraries
date:
Posted On:
                19 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR) successfully organised a two-week skill training programme on “Skill Training in Library Automation, Digitization and Artificial Intelligence for Libraries” during 5–16 October 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). Organised by the Institute’s Training Division, the programme aimed to strengthen the technical competencies of library and information science professionals, academicians, researchers, students and IT professionals in library automation, digitisation, digital repository management and the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in library services. A total of 16 participants from universities, research institutions, libraries, and other organizations across the country attended the programme.
Dr. Geeta Vani Rasayam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, inaugurated the programme and encouraged participants to actively engage in the training. Shri Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, introduced the objectives of the programme and highlighted the importance of skill development in library automation, digitisation and the adoption of emerging technologies. Shri Salim Ansari moderated the inaugural session.
Designed with an emphasis on experiential learning, the programme combined expert lectures, demonstrations and hands-on sessions on Koha Integrated Library Management System (ILMS) and DSpace digital repository software.
The Koha sessions covered open-source software fundamentals, installation of the Linux operating system and Koha, catalogue management, patron management, circulation workflows, report generation, system customisation, and backup and restoration. Participants gained practical experience in configuring and managing library automation functions and workflows.
The DSpace sessions focused on installation and administration, management of communities and collections, item submission, e-people registration and authorisation, Dublin Core and Bitstream Registry management, basic customisation, and backup and restoration. These sessions provided practical exposure to digital repository management for the organisation, preservation and dissemination of scholarly and institutional knowledge.
The programme also covered emerging applications of Artificial Intelligence in libraries, including AI tools and metadata extraction using AI. A special session on iThenticate was conducted on 15 October 2026 to familiarise participants with text similarity checking and its relevance to responsible academic and scholarly writing.
As part of the programme, participants visited the National Science Library to gain insights into its resources and services. The academic sessions were conducted by Shri Mukesh Pund, Shri Sanjay Burde, Dr. Avinash Kshitij, Shri Salim Ansari and Shri Bharath Natarajan. The practical exercises enabled participants to apply the concepts covered during the training.
The valedictory session acknowledged the participants’ engagement and encouraged them to apply the knowledge and practical skills acquired during the training in their respective institutions. The programme was coordinated by Ms. Meetali Bharti, Programme Coordinator and Nodal Principal Investigator (PI), with Mr. Salim Ansari, Co-PI and Course Co-Coordinator, and Mr. Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division and Course Coordinator.
Through the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III), CSIR-NIScPR continues to strengthen professional capacity in library and information science and promote the adoption of open-source technologies and Artificial Intelligence in library services, contributing to the modernisation of libraries and digital knowledge management across academic and research institutions.

“Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas”
, the Minister underscored the importance of a
whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach
to social empowerment.
He advised officers to strengthen coordination with the Social Welfare Departments of States and Union Territories, as well as other relevant stakeholders, to facilitate smooth, seamless and effective implementation of welfare schemes.
Dr. Kumar directed senior officers to work diligently, carefully and proactively in formulating and implementing schemes, programmes, initiatives and action plans that respond to the needs of all stakeholders. He stressed that effective coordination, regular monitoring and timely corrective measures are essential to overcome implementation gaps and ensure that the intended benefits of government interventions reach eligible individuals and communities across the country.
The Minister also emphasised the need for greater public awareness of the Ministry’s schemes and programmes through systematic dissemination of information on their objectives, eligibility criteria, benefits and application procedures. He called upon officers to ensure that prospective beneficiaries receive clear, accessible and timely information so that eligible individuals can avail themselves of the benefits for which they qualify.

title: A Success Story under NAMASTE
subtitle: From Sanitation Workers to Mechanised Service Entrepreneurs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Access to financial assistance and modern equipment creates new opportunities for sanitation workers to improve their livelihoods and achieve financial independence.
The journey of T. Ravi Kumar, P. Sekhar, T. Nikhil and E. Ailaiah from Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, demonstrates how collective entrepreneurship and mechanisation can help sanitation workers build sustainable livelihoods while promoting safer and more efficient sanitation services.
The four beneficiaries were engaged in sanitation work and aspired to improve their income and working conditions by adopting mechanised sanitation services. However, the high cost of modern equipment, coupled with limited access to finance, made it difficult for them to purchase machinery individually. Despite their experience in the sanitation sector, financial constraints restricted their ability to expand their livelihood opportunities and achieve greater economic stability for their families.
A significant change began when the beneficiaries attended an awareness camp organised by the Nellore Municipal Corporation, where they learned about the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) under the NAMASTE Scheme. The scheme opened up an opportunity for them to pursue their shared goal of establishing a mechanised sanitation service through a group project. With financial assistance in the form of a bank loan and upfront capital subsidy, they procured a Mini Jetting Machine to undertake mechanised sewer and septic tank cleaning services.
The total project cost was Rs 35.85 lakh, of which Rs 21.89 lakh was financed through a bank loan and Rs 13.96 lakh was provided as capital subsidy. This support enabled the beneficiaries to overcome the initial financial barrier and acquire modern sanitation equipment that would otherwise have remained beyond their individual means.
Following the procurement of the machine, the Nellore Municipal Corporation engaged the group’s equipment on a long-term basis, with monthly hiring charges of approximately Rs 78,500. This arrangement provided a regular source of revenue and created a more sustainable livelihood opportunity for all four beneficiaries. After meeting operational expenses, each group member now earns approximately Rs 37,000 per month, significantly strengthening their financial position and ability to meet household needs.
The intervention has enabled the beneficiaries to move beyond the limitations of traditional sanitation work and become owner-operators of mechanised sanitation equipment. Their improved earnings have contributed to greater financial stability, while access to mechanisation supports safer and more efficient sanitation operations. The opportunity to work collectively has also demonstrated the value of group entrepreneurship in overcoming financial barriers and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities.
Supported during 2021–22, the group’s journey reflects the transformative potential of the Swachhta Udyami Yojana under NAMASTE. By facilitating access to capital, modern equipment and assured work opportunities, the initiative has helped T. Ravi Kumar, P. Sekhar, T. Nikhil and E. Ailaiah strengthen their livelihoods, enhance their occupational dignity and work towards a more secure future for their families. Their success illustrates how targeted financial assistance and mechanisation can empower sanitation workers to become entrepreneurs while contributing to improved sanitation services.

title: NFSC Fellowship: Supporting Dr Shrikant Dilip Khandare’s Journey to Ph.D. Completion
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Higher education and advanced research open pathways to academic excellence, professional growth and meaningful contributions to society. With the right support and encouragement, scholars from SC, ST, OBC & other such backgrounds become empowered to pursue their research aspirations, strengthen their knowledge and skills, and work towards achieving their academic goals.
Financial assistance plays a vital role in enabling them to focus on their studies, explore their potential and build a strong foundation for future success.
Dr Shrikant Dilip Khandare, a scholar from Solapur, Maharashtra, pursued his doctoral studies with the aim of contributing to sustainable solutions for environmental challenges. After qualifying the CSIR-UGC NET in June 2018, he continued to work towards his academic aspirations. However, financial uncertainty posed challenges to the continuation of his research and created concerns about completing his Ph.D.
Coming from a family whose circumstances were described as unstable, Dr Khandare faced uncertainty about sustaining his doctoral studies. Despite his determination to continue his research, financial constraints threatened his academic progress. He acknowledged that, without financial assistance, he might have had to discontinue his doctoral programme. Nevertheless, he remained committed to pursuing his research and achieving his academic goals.
Financial assistance under the
National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC)
became an important source of support in Dr Khandare’s academic journey. He began receiving assistance in October 2019, including fellowship support and House Rent Allowance (HRA), amounting to a total of ₹9.90 lakh. This assistance helped him continue his doctoral studies and devote greater attention to his academic work without the constant uncertainty of financing his education.
With the support received under the NFSC scheme and his sustained commitment to research, Dr Khandare successfully completed his Ph.D. The fellowship played a significant role in enabling him to continue his doctoral programme and achieve this important academic milestone. His experience highlights how timely financial assistance can help scholars overcome economic barriers and pursue advanced education.
Dr Khandare’s research aspirations are closely connected to addressing environmental challenges, particularly plastic waste and pollution. He aims to contribute to the development of sustainable solutions to tackle these issues. His academic journey reflects the potential of research and higher education to support environmental sustainability and generate knowledge that can contribute to addressing pressing societal concerns.
Dr Shrikant Dilip Khandare’s achievement demonstrates the importance of fellowship assistance in strengthening access to higher education and research. His journey illustrates how targeted financial support, combined with perseverance and academic commitment, can help scholars navigate financial uncertainty, complete doctoral studies and work towards their research ambitions. The NFSC scheme continues to represent an important avenue for supporting eligible Scheduled Caste students in pursuing advanced education and research.

title: Pumped Storage Hydropower
subtitle: Powering India's Clean Energy Transition
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 OCT 2026 11:02AM by PIB Delhi
content:
As clean energy reshapes India's power landscape, a timeless technology is paving the way for a powerful new energy future. Often described as a water battery, pumped storage uses water and gravity to store electricity, bridging the gap between when power is generated and when it is needed. From reservoirs to modern grids, it is helping shape a cleaner, more reliable and resilient energy future.
Building India's Energy Future with Storage
India’s energy transition is increasingly anchored in renewable energy to strengthen energy security and sustainability. The country is rapidly expanding solar and wind capacity to meet rising electricity demand with cleaner sources. As of July 2026, India has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity. During FY 2025–26, India added around 55.29 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity. India has also set a target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Solar and wind energy are going to make major contributions towards achieving this target
.
However, renewable energy generation varies with sunlight, weather and daily demand patterns. This variability creates a growing need to store electricity when renewable generation exceeds demand. Energy storage can then supply electricity during periods of low renewable generation or peak demand.
As renewable capacity expands, the requirement for energy storage would also increase rapidly. The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) projects 73.93 GW of storage capacity by 2031–32. This includes 26.69 GW from Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) and 47.24 GW from Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
PSPs can play a crucial role in meeting this long-duration storage requirement. PSPs store electricity by pumping water to an upper reservoir during periods of surplus generation. The stored water is released through turbines when electricity demand rises. This enables PSPs to shift renewable electricity across time and support grid stability. They also provide long-duration storage and peaking support, making them important for integrating large renewable capacities.
Types of Energy Storage
Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) offer complementary solutions for integrating renewable energy into the grid.
BESS can respond rapidly to short-duration requirements
,
supporting frequency regulation, peak management and grid balancing. PSPs provide
long-duration storage
, shifting large quantities of electricity across periods of surplus and demand. BESS can be deployed relatively quickly and close to renewable generation or consumption centres. PSPs require suitable geographical conditions but can provide large-scale storage over extended periods. Their long operating life also supports sustained grid infrastructure needs.
Understanding PSPs: Cycle of Energy Storage and Supply
A Pumped Storage Project typically consists of two reservoirs located at different elevations. During periods of surplus electricity, water is pumped from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir, where energy is stored as potential energy. When electricity is required, water is released from the upper reservoir through turbines to generate electricity. Once demand subsides, water is pumped back to the upper reservoir during periods of surplus electricity, completing the storage cycle. Pumped Storage Projects therefore function as large-scale energy storage systems and contribute to grid stability and renewable energy integration.
Categorising Pumped Storage Power Plants
PSPs are classified according to how their reservoirs are connected to, or situated in relation to, natural watercourses. They are grouped into three types:
on-stream, off-stream open-loop and off-stream closed-loop schemes
. These configurations reflect the varying association between a project’s reservoirs and natural watercourses.
On-stream Pumped Storage
On-stream pumped storage schemes
have
both reservoirs located on a river, stream or nallah.
To meet the electricity demands, water stored in the upper reservoir flows through turbines to generate electricity. During periods of low electricity demand or surplus power, water is pumped back to the upper reservoir for reuse.
Off-stream Open-loop Pumped Storage
Off-stream open-loop pumped storage schemes have
one reservoir located on a river, stream or nallah. In contrast, the other reservoir is not located on a river, a perennial stream, or a perennial nallah
. When electricity is required, water flows from the upper reservoir through turbines to produce electricity. Surplus electricity is subsequently used to pump the water back, restoring the system for another cycle.
Off-stream Closed-loop Pumped Storage
Neither reservoir in an off-stream closed-loop pumped storage scheme is located on a river, perennial stream or perennial nallah.
Both reservoirs are situated away from perennial natural watercourses. When electricity is required, water flows from the upper reservoir through turbines that generate power, and is then pumped back to the upper reservoir during periods of low electricity demand or surplus power.
All three types of Pumped Storage Projects have a role based on site-specific geographical and technical conditions. However, efforts are being made to identify more off-stream projects located away from rivers, supporting faster project execution and minimising impacts on aquatic ecology and the surrounding environment.
Scaling Up Energy Storage: India's Pumped Storage Momentum
India is rapidly expanding its pumped storage capacity to support its growing renewable energy base. The development is progressing across operational, construction and pre-construction stages. This expanding pipeline is strengthening India’s long-duration energy storage infrastructure.
Operational Capacity:
As of August 2026, India has 7.43 GW of operational PSP capacity
across 10 projects.
The projects have installed
capacity
above 25 MW.
Under Construction/ implementation Stage:
A further 15.87 GW across 11 PSPs is under construction and/or under implementation across the country.
Next Stage of
Pipeline:
10.40 GW across 8 projects has been concurred
or appraised by the Central Electricity Authority.
India's Regionally Diverse Pumped Storage Potential
India has identified 320 pumped storage projects with a combined potential of 345.38 GW. This includes 62 on-stream projects with 56.67 GW and 258 off-stream projects with 288.71 GW. These projects span all five regions and include different stages of development,
including projects already in operation
.
PSP development and site suitability require assessment of several technical and environmental aspects. These include topography, geology, hydrology, reservoir characteristics, foundation conditions, seismicity and environmental considerations. Construction materials, power potential and transmission connectivity are also examined during project appraisal.
The Western Region has the highest identified potential at 129.72 GW. CEA attributes this mainly to topographical features and steep gradients of rivers originating from the Western Ghats.
Maharashtra accounts for 67.36 GW, followed by Gujarat with 33.36 GW.
The
Southern Region
has 97.76 GW, led by Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu. The
Eastern Region
has 53.41 GW, including 41.53 GW in Odisha. The
Northern Region
has 50.32 GW, led by Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh. The
North Eastern Region
contributes 14.18 GW to the identified national potential. Collectively, these regional resources underline the scale and spread of India’s pumped storage opportunity.
Projected Capacity Addition of Pumped Storage Projects
This extensive resource base provides a strong foundation for scaling long-duration energy storage. The Central Electricity Authority has therefore mapped a substantial capacity addition pathway through 2035–36.
Projects totalling 100.81 GW are envisaged for commissioning by 2035–36.
This includes projects already under construction and would take cumulative PSP capacity to 105.56 GW. The planned expansion can significantly strengthen grid flexibility and enable greater integration of renewable energy. It also positions pumped storage as an important pillar of India’s future electricity system.

Global Installed Capacity PSPs
Pumped Storage Hydropower Is the world's most widely deployed form of large-scale energy storage, reflecting its established scale and maturity relative to other storage technologies. Global installed pumped hydro capacity stood at
159.8 Gigawatts at the end of 2025
, according to the
International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA
).
China
accounted for nearly
66 Gigawatts
of this capacity, followed by
Japan
and the
United States
with around
22 Gigawatts and 19 Gigawatts
, respectively.
India ranks fourth globally
in installed pumped storage capacity, with
7.18 Gigawatts at the end of 2025
. The country's capacity has since increased to
7.43 Gigawatts as of July 2026
, reinforcing its growing role in the global pumped storage landscape.
Government Initiatives and Measures
The Government of India has taken a series of coordinated policy, regulatory, demand-side and supply-side measures to promote the development and deployment of PSPs.
Dedicated PSP Development Guidelines:
The Ministry of Power notified the
Guidelines to Promote Development of Pumped Storage Projects in India
in April 2023.
The guidelines provide a policy framework for facilitating faster PSP development.
Click to Access Guideline
Support for Enabling Infrastructure:
Budgetary support covers essential infrastructure required for PSP development. This includes roads, bridges, railway sidings, ropeways, communication facilities and transmission lines. These measures improve project connectivity and strengthen project viability.
Competitive Procurement Framework:
Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) Guidelines were notified in February 2025. They provide a transparent and standardised framework for procuring storage capacity and stored energy from PSPs.
Inter-State Transmission System Charge Waiver:
PSPs awarded for construction by 30 June 2028 are eligible for a 100% ISTS charge waiver. The waiver applies for 25 years from commercial operation. This measure strengthens the financial viability of PSPs.
Faster Project Approvals:
Revised CEA guidelines have reduced Detailed Project Report concurrence timelines. The timeline has been reduced from 90 days to 50 days for all PSPs. The requirement for clearance of Inter-State Aspects has also been removed. These measures support faster project development.
Streamlined Environmental Appraisal:
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has introduced differentiated appraisal provisions for PSPs. Eligible projects can benefit from B2 categorisation under the applicable provisions. Off-stream projects also benefit from reduced baseline data requirements. These measures can accelerate environmental appraisal while maintaining regulatory safeguards.
Facilitating Survey and Investigation:
MoEF&CC extended forest land survey provisions and enhanced borehole exploration limits for PSPs, facilitating timely preparation of technically robust Detailed Project Reports.
Integrated Grid and Transmission Planning:
National electricity planning integrates energy storage and transmission development. This approach addresses renewable energy variability, reduces congestion and strengthens grid reliability. A roadmap envisages integrating 100 GW of PSP capacity between 2025–26 and 2035–36.
Digital Project Monitoring:
The Central Electricity Authority’s Jal Vidyut DPR portal enables real-time monitoring of survey and investigation activities. It also facilitates coordination among stakeholders during project preparation. This digital approach helps streamline approvals and accelerate PSP development.
Review of limit of capital expenditure requiring the concurrence of the CEA:
Government of India, vide Gazette Notification dated 01.08.2025, has revised the capital expenditure limit for schemes related to setting up hydro generating stations to ₹3,000 crore, requiring the concurrence of the CEA. Further, off-stream closed-loop pumped storage schemes, irrespective of the quantum of capital expenditure have been exempted from the requirement of concurrence by the CEA
These measures spanning policy clarity, fiscal support, streamlined clearances, competitive procurement and integrated grid planning have created an enabling environment for the accelerated development of PSPs.
Energy Transition's Next Imperative
India's target of achieving 500 Gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 represents a fundamental shift in the country's electricity landscape. As renewable energy assumes a larger role, the ability to store energy and deploy it in line with demand will become increasingly important for maintaining a reliable and balanced power system. Pumped Storage Hydropower is well positioned to address this requirement through its ability to provide large-scale, long-duration energy storage while supporting a range of wider power system needs. Its role extends from managing peak demand and integrating variable renewable energy to strengthening grid flexibility and resilience. As the clean energy ecosystem continues to evolve, the effective deployment of energy storage alongside generation and transmission infrastructure will be central to building a power system that is cleaner, more flexible and prepared for the future.

date:

content:
The National Human Rights Commission has announced the 10 winners of its online 'Human Rights Quiz-2026: Celebrating Life, Liberty, Equality and Dignity'. It was organised in collaboration with MyGov from 1st September to 10th October 2026 in the run-up to its 33rd Foundation Day. The quiz sought to engage everyone in learning about human rights, the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993 and the functions, powers and duties of the NHRC in promoting and protecting human rights across the country.
The 1st prize of Rs.15,000/- has been won by Ms. Aarti Mahajan. The 2nd prize of Rs.10,000/- has been won by Ms. Ritika and the 3rd prize of Rs.5,000/- has gone to Ms. Tooba Benazeer. The seven consolation prizes of Rs.2,000/- each have gone to Shri Aditya Gupta, Shri Tarun, Shri Rani Mandal, Shri Basant Kumar Mahato, Shri Likhth Kumar A and Ms. Deepika Madasu.
The quiz saw participation from all States and Union Territories (UTs) of the country. It attracted 1,67,127 views with 26,459 submissions. Out of them, most submissions were in the age group of 18-24. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu topped the state-wise participation.
5,753 participants secured 15 out of 15 score, of which the 10 winners were decided by a draw of lots by the MyGov team as per the terms and conditions of the quiz.
Participants were required to answer a maximum of 15 questions within 300 seconds.
